cite: Bridge, seawall and waterfront fishing bans in 16 Florida codes, checked 12 Nov 2026
title: Bans on fishing from bridges, seawalls and waterfront facilities do not reach a spearfisher in the water (confirmed negative, with one caution)
effect: These sections bar fishing from a bridge, seawall, street or waterfront facility, or loitering on it; none bars spearing in the water around it: Bal Harbour § 10-1, Belleair § 34-6, Deerfield Beach § 46-4, Fort Lauderdale §§ 16-74 and 8-5, Hallandale Beach § 19-12, Key Colony Beach § 5-9, Martin County § 83.1, Miami-Dade County § 7-3, Monroe County §§ 19-3 and 19-5, Ocean Ridge § 38-5, Tequesta § 54-6, Treasure Island § 58-35, Town of Palm Beach § 74-163, Oakland Park § 8-5 and Wilton Manors § 12-4. Caution: the statewide 100 yd spearfishing buffer of r. 68B-20.003(2)(c) attaches only where public fishing from the bridge is legally permitted, so a bridge where fishing is banned (Card Sound, Sadowski Causeway, Tom's Harbor Channel) arguably has no such buffer. The map still draws the buffer at every bridge, the reading that closes more water. Bal Harbour § 10-1 also bars fishing in any area of the village posted against fishing, and Cocoa Beach § 5-30 bars fishing within 50 ft of the centre of any posted bridge; both sit inside the statewide bridge buffer as drawn.
excerpt: (a) There shall be no fishing from the Card Sound Bridge in Monroe County, Florida.
scope: The jurisdictions named.
note: Found 12 Nov 2026 by the whole-state 'fishing from / in / within' Municode search and read through the content service. The excerpt is Monroe County § 19-3(a), as an example of the form. Other sections from that search with no bearing on spearing: Hernando County § 21-1 (nets and crab traps in canals), Naples §§ 42-53 and 28-34 (pier and park conduct), St. Augustine Beach § 5-4 (county pier conduct), Volusia County § 20-116 (ocean fishing after a Beach Patrol warning; chumming within 600 ft), Venice § 46-63 and Bradenton Beach § 66-60 (no fishing in swimming areas).
